slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 22:8: Abraham answered, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.’
slides.body: “Abraham answered, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.’”
slides.heading: Gen 22:8

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the link between God's provision in Genesis 22 and John's Lamb of God.
slides.body: Abraham says God will provide the lamb. A ram then dies instead of Isaac. John later calls Jesus ‘the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.’
slides.heading: Did God promise Jesus as the lamb?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the substitutionary Christian typology of Isaac and Jesus.
slides.body: A beloved son faces death; God provides a substitute; the victim dies in the son's place. Christians see the whole pattern—not just one word—as anticipating God's ultimate provision in Jesus.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three distinguishes Genesis's immediate resolution from later Christian typology.
slides.body: Genesis provides a ram for that day's offering. John never cites Isaac, and his lamb image may also evoke Passover and Isaiah 53. This is powerful, coherent typology—but not a uniquely identifiable prediction.
slides.heading: The story supplies its own answer

title: Did Abraham promise Jesus as God's lamb?
